title: The panel shows the panes that matter, and you can say which
goal: The panel now carries so many sections that it is hard to read and hard to predict, and some of them are almost never wanted. Let the panel show only what is worth showing: an automatic mode that offers the sections the thing you picked actually needs, and a way at the bottom to say which of the questionable ones you want to see.
notes:
The user's words: 'I feel like we should maybe have a way to not show some panes. I think the library pane will almost never be used. But maybe at the bottom of the panel is a way to show/hide panes that are questionably necessary so we can have an auto mode that only shows panes relevant to the situation.'

This is the same instinct as the modes work ('work-out-whether-the-app-needs-project-types-at', where a mode is a preset of what is visible and you can always turn a hidden thing back on). Read that task: if modes land, per-pane visibility is part of what a mode IS, and these two must not grow separate machinery for one idea. Say in the log which way that was resolved.

The automatic rule is the part worth thinking hardest about, because 'relevant to the situation' is easy to say and easy to get wrong. A section that appears and disappears as the selection changes makes the panel unpredictable, which is one of the things the user is already complaining about. Hiding a rarely wanted section permanently is predictable; showing and hiding sections per selection may be worse than the clutter. Weigh that honestly rather than assuming automatic is better.

---
Said by the user on 2026-09-15, looking at the panel with a component selected:

"the number of panes is obnoxious. why would i ever care to set position and width manually? this kind of shit is really front and foreground rather than using the component instance. And i hate input box grids, it's the laziest ui possible. First, I don't need position in the pane at all. if I want to move something i use the V tool. If we want precision placement right click and have an option to do that. Same with sizing. Paddings should have a simplified way to set paddings with one row, like maybe an input and a little dropdown next to it. type 14, you get 14 on all sides, hit the dropdown and a popout lets you type individual values and input shows 'mixed' or something. But the panes are now completely cluttered and hard to read and unpredictable. total mess. I feel like we should maybe have a way to not show some panes. I think the library pane will almost never be used. But maybe at the bottom of the panel is a way to show/hide panes that are questionably necessary so we can have an auto mode that only shows panes relevant to the situation"

THIS IS MEASURED, NOT JUST FELT. The study 'work-out-whether-the-right-hand-pane-is-carrying' (done, 2026-09-15) measured the dock in the running app: 1052 points of sections against a 968 point viewport at 1680x1000, and Position & Size never wholly on screen at any window size. Its page is docs/design/mocks/pages/pane-load.html and its audit is queue/audits/2026-09-15-pane-load.json. Read both before starting: the measuring is done and should not be redone.

The four threads are filed as four tasks because they are four different fixes, but they are one complaint and whoever picks one up should read the others.
acceptance: There is a way, at the foot of the panel, to choose which sections are shown, and it is unobtrusive rather than another section
An automatic mode shows the sections relevant to what is picked and leaves the rest out, and what counts as relevant is written down rather than decided case by case
Nothing becomes unreachable: a section that is hidden can be brought back without hunting, and the audit shows how
The choice is remembered between launches, and per release, the way other panel state already is
The Library section in particular is out of the way by default, since it is the clearest example of a section that is rarely wanted while a layer is selected
The panel is measurably shorter for a typical selection: before and after heights in points, for a shape, a piece of text and a component copy

It agrees with the rule about what opens when you pick something rather than fighting it: read 'picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t' first, which is the open question about whether picking should move the panel at all
Somebody who hides everything is not left with an empty panel and no way back
Audit under queue/audits/ with the panel in automatic mode for three different selections, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. (1) The panel ALREADY only draws the sections the selection makes available (InspectorPanel.availableSections is one long selection-driven test per section), so a naive 'auto mode that shows what is relevant' adds a label and nothing else. What it lacks is the ability to say 'I never want this one', and a written-down rule for the questionable ones. (2) The task's own warning is right: a section that comes and goes as you click from layer to layer is WORSE than the clutter. So Automatic is constrained by a rule I can state in one sentence — what you PICK never adds or removes an optional section; only what the DOCUMENT holds, the tool in your hand, and what you asked for may. Every automatic answer below is a document-level or tool-level fact. (3) The bootstrap trap: if Motion is hidden until the document holds a motion, you cannot make the first one. The foot of the panel is the way in, one click, and it is always on screen because it sits outside the dock's scroller. (4) Shortest version that delivers the value: one override map (section id -> shown), default absent meaning automatic. No global Automatic/Custom mode toggle — per-section overrides are strictly more useful (pin Measurements on forever, let everything else be automatic) and are exactly the machinery a MODE preset will later set.

MODES: resolved the way the task's notes asked. This task builds the machinery and 'work-out-whether-the-app-needs-project-types-at' (still pending, still a mock study) will use it. PanelSectionVisibility.Choices IS what a mode is a preset of: a named set of the same per-section answers, set in one go. Written into docs/design/panel-sections.md under 'This is what a MODE is made of', with the instruction that a mode needing to hide something not in the optional list widens THAT list rather than adding a parallel switch. No second mechanism.

AGREES WITH THE DOCK RULE rather than fighting it (acceptance 7). Read 'picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t' first: it is done, its card was answered 'What you picked sits at the top', and the settled rule is that the ORDER puts the pick on screen and a pick NEVER scrolls the dock. Nothing here touches the order or adds a reveal. The one rule this adds sits beside it and is written into InspectorDockLayout.swift's rule block under the same heading: the order decides where a section sits, this decides whether there is one. Because a Situation carries no selection at all, a pick cannot add or remove a section either, which is the same instinct the order rule was chosen for.

THE HONEST FINDING, and it is in the audit and the design doc too: the automatic half saves very little on its own. The panel was ALREADY selection-driven, and for most optional sections the automatic answer and the existing applicability test say the same thing (Measurements only ever applied with a measurement in the document, Component only with a component involved). Writing them down as one readable rule is worth doing and the next section added now has to answer the question rather than invent an answer, but it moves few points. The value delivered is the other half of what was asked for: you can say 'I never want Layout' and it sticks, per release, forever.

CAUGHT BEFORE SHIPPING: Motion's automatic rule was first written as 'the document already moves, or the timing strip is open', which was the single biggest saving available (130pt on EVERY picked layer). It is a bug. The plus on the Motion section's own header is how the first motion is made, and hasMotionStrip is false until document.hasMotion, so hiding the section leaves NOTHING in the window that could start an animation, and motion-swings-a-layer-walk fails on its first step (it expects 'Motion Empty' present). Motion is now hideable but never automatically hidden. documentHasMotion and isTimingStripShown were removed from Situation rather than left as facts nothing reads.

PERF, since the panel asks this on every draw: EditorState.panelSectionSituation walks children with an early exit instead of Document.allLayers, which allocates a new array holding a copy of every layer in the document. The two height-record guards in InspectorPanel now test availableSections rather than orderedAvailableSections, so the geometry callbacks that fire on every scroll tick do not walk the document at all.
